static_traits.name: Gu Rui
static_traits.family_status: Has a daughter; other family situations Not mentioned
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with friends are affected (self-isolates to avoid being hurt again); has a best friend living in the same neighborhood; friends and younger sister provide support
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no similar psychological problems before, has not received psychological counseling yet; ankle injured while walking a week ago
static_traits.language_features: Positive attitude, willing to cooperate (indicating 'ready'); slightly Anxious; clear expression; tendency to overanalyze; skeptical about positive feedback

basic_info.main_problem: Ankle injured during the last walk, since then developing Self-blame and guilt due to not being more cautious, negative Automatic thoughts appearing daily, affecting daily activities and physical/mental pleasure; while Anxiety and Self-doubt persistently appear in cooking situations.
basic_info.core_demands: Seeking help because self-blame and negative thinking affect mental health and enjoyment of daily activities, hoping to challenge and correct unreasonable thoughts through counseling, gaining a more balanced perspective and improving experiences.
growth_experiences: Years ago when cooking for guests at a dinner party, burning a dish, the whole gathering was subjectively experienced by the client as a 'disaster'. Since then, every cooking became tense and Anxious, the client often has Self-doubt while cooking (such as 'I will definitely mess up' 'I do not cook well'), and views small mistakes (such as too much salt, slightly overcooked) as whole-meal failure. Even when others give positive feedback, the client tends to think the other is only being polite or comforting, thus negating positive feedback. This event has had a lasting impact on her daily life and self-evaluation.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough(easily viewing small mistakes as overall failure)
Making mistakes means I have problems/am irresponsible

special_situations.event: Ankle injured during the last walk (not yet seeing the pothole in advance)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I had not spotted the risk in advance and avoided the injury, it means I am irresponsible, I should have done better
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Overly cautious while walking, slows down, even avoids going out to prevent being injured again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have been more careful, It is all my fault

special_situations.event: Cooking for others/recalling the burned dish at the past dinner party
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one dish has an error, it means the whole meal is a failure, I am a terrible Chef
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding cooking for others; strictly relying on new recipes and seeking others' verification to reduce mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely mess up, I am a lousy Chef

special_situations.event: Others' positive feedback or praise for the dishes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' praise is only politeness not genuine affirmation, only complete flawlessness counts as truly good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive feedback, continuing self-criticism, maintaining high standards to pursue 'zero mistakes'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite, do not really like it

special_situations.event: Seeing others walk or do physical activity
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I participate in similar activities, I am very likely to get injured again, so I should avoid them
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces or avoids physical activity, keeps distance from friends to lower risk
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I go and attend, something will happen / I will be hurt again

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and seen as competent (including as a cook and a father), and hopes to stay in control and reduce mistakes
core_conflict.fear: Fearing mistakes causing others' disappointment or negative evaluations, or getting injured again; worrying about being seen as incompetent
defense_goal: Maintains control and improvement through self-criticism
Avoiding high-risk activities or Cooking for others to lower the possibility of being evaluated and injured
Suppressing emotions through overanalysis and rationalization, relieving Anxiety

object_relations.self_representation: making mistakes easily, a 'terrible Chef/incompetent person' who needs perfection
object_relations.object_representation: Others are harsh critics or superficially polite comforters

object_relations.self_representation: a Father worried about disappointing his daughter
object_relations.object_representation: Family/children who may be disappointed and doubt one's ability

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others praise one's dishes or give positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to think the other is only being polite or comforting, the real evaluation may be not good (transference: projecting inner negation onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone gentle, first accepting the other's feedback, then probing evidence with open-ended questions (such as 'which specific part do you like?'), avoiding immediate negation; moderately self-disclosing current unease.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Preparing to Cook for others or recalling the burned-dish situation at the dinner party
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizing the outside's high standards and 'zero mistakes' rules, believing small mistakes equal overall failure (transference: the harsh others of Introjection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use a supportive tone, inviting distinguishing 'external standards' from 'personally feasible standards'; encouraging concretizing the impact scope of mistakes, Guiding to see partial successes and improvement points.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Seeing others do physical activity or recalling details of the ankle injury
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Avoids emotions through rational detailing and over-analysis, presetting the possibility of being injured again (transference: amplifying the sense of danger)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Keeping a steady pace and Empathic tone, first mirroring her worries, then Guiding back to concrete present body signals and safety behaviors; replacing lengthy analysis with small-step behavioral experiments.

Relationship with friends affected, Reduced socializing activities
outcomes: Decreased enjoyment of life, reduced activities

manifestations: The joy of cooking swallowed by Persistent self-doubt and 'zero mistakes' standards
Treats a small mistake as failure of the whole meal; hard to gain a sense of meaning from positive feedback
outcomes: Avoiding Cooking for others, increased pressure at family meals

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using self-Demands of 'should/must be more careful'
Treats zero mistakes as the only standard, errors mean failure

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-scrutiny and criticism before and after cooking
Quickly Self-denying when facing praise, finding it hard to accept positive information

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Believing others' praise is only politeness or comfort, not genuinely liking it
Infers others' negative evaluations of him without evidence

Recalling the burnt-dish experience at a past dinner party
Others present or Anticipating being evaluated

target_behavior.function: Avoiding being evaluated, maintaining control and Self-protection (lowering Anxiety in the short term)
target_behavior.consequence: Losing the joy of cooking, avoiding Cooking for others, Increased stress at family meals

Being asked by others about injuries/safety

target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety worsened, reduced activities, emotional distress affecting daily functioning

Planning to go out or thinking about the possibility of getting hurt again

target_behavior.consequence: Reduced physical activity, Interpersonal relationships becoming distant, decreased life enjoyment
